name: SE_XMLImportText
summary: Loads text pages from XML text (<language><page><t>) into the VM text tables.
semantics: Parses arg1 as XML TEXT (the document contents, not a file name) with libxml (Script::LoadPckXml -> xmlReadMemory). Parse failure (NULL doc) -> 0. Takes the root element (xmlDocGetRootElement) and walks it and its siblings for the first ELEMENT named 'language' (case-insensitive); in practice the root element itself must be <language id="N">; none found -> 0. Script::ParseLanguageElement: attribute id (atol); if id>0, for every child element named 'page' (case-insens.) ParsePageXml(vm, id, page): page id attr (atol) is mapped (380000..399999 -> id-380000, 350000..379999 -> id-350000, 300001..349999 -> id-300000, otherwise unchanged); every child <t id="K">text</t> (element name 't', case-insens.) is stored with text = node content passed through UnescapeTextPageString (rules: see SE_ConvertTextString) and its stored length, into the language slot vm+0x334+id*4 (StoreTextPageEntries; existing ids of that page are replaced/added). Returns 1 when a language element was found and parsed, else 0. The libxml doc is freed afterwards.
notes: Handler 0x4ae659 (case 0). A non-string arg1 leaves a NULL pointer that is passed straight to strlen/xmlReadMemory (no type check) -> access violation. Used to load language files as strings.

name: SE_ReadText
summary: Returns a text from the loaded text pages by (page, id) or (page, language, id); a placeholder "ReadText..." when missing.
semantics: Arg forms by argc. argc==1: page=0, id=arg1. argc==2: page=arg1, id=arg2, language=current (EngineConfig+0x76c). argc==3: page=arg1, LANGUAGE=arg2 (index into vm textPages), id=arg3. Found: result = CopyCell of the stored text cell (a string cell). Not found, or textPages[lang] is NULL: result is a freshly built string 'ReadText<id>' (argc 1), 'ReadText<page>-<id>' (argc 2), 'ReadText<page>-<lang>-<id>' (argc 3) (%d formatting of the raw int values, SprintfBuf50 so max 49 chars). Values are read as raw dwords, types are not checked. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B148 (3-arg language outside 0..998 answers as a language without pages)
bugs: AP 0x004ac003: the 3-arg language id indexes vm.textPages[999] unchecked (crash on a bad id). Fixed in x3_src (B148).
notes: Text lookup: Gui::FindTextEntryInPage(textPages[lang], page, id) = hash on page id, then binary search by text id; returns the entry's payload cell. textPages[] is vm+0x334, 'lang' index = EngineConfig+0x76c (current language) unless given. Note the argc==3 order: (page, language, id); the language is arg 2, not arg 1. Strings returned from the page are NOT run through ExpandTextReferences.

name: SE_ExistsText
summary: Returns the text if a text entry exists (truthy), else 0.
semantics: Same argument forms and lookup as SE_ReadText (argc 1: page 0,id; argc 2: page,id with current language; argc 3: page,lang,id). If the entry is found the result is a CopyCell of the text cell itself (the string, NOT int 1). If not found or textPages[lang] is NULL the result is int 0. No fallback string.
bugs: AP 0x004ac14c: same unchecked language index as SE_ReadText (B148, fixed in x3_src).
notes: Text lookup: Gui::FindTextEntryInPage(textPages[lang], page, id) = hash on page id, then binary search by text id; returns the entry's payload cell. textPages[] is vm+0x334, 'lang' index = EngineConfig+0x76c (current language) unless given. So the script-visible truthiness is: found -> the (usually non-empty) string; missing -> 0.

name: SE_LoadText
summary: No-op stub: loads nothing, returns 0 (texts come from SE_XMLImportText / startup).
semantics: Release-build stub: arguments are ignored and int 0 is returned at once (AP shared stub 0x004acdaa, also SE_Assert; FL shared stub 0x004cbdc6 for all the no-op SE natives). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_LoadTextPage
summary: No-op stub: loads nothing, returns 0.
semantics: Release-build stub: arguments are ignored and int 0 is returned at once (AP shared stub 0x004abd24, also SE_LoadTextPage/Trace/ShowCallStack/DumpValues/UpdateStory; FL shared stub 0x004cbdc6). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_GetLanguage
summary: Returns the current game language id (e.g. 44 English, 49 German, 7 Russian).
semantics: Returns the current game language id: the dword at Init::g_pEngineConfig(0x00606f34)+0x76c (same numbers as the language ids of the text files, e.g. 44 English, 49 German, 33 French, 7 Russian). Pure read, no args.
notes: Handler 0x4ac1d9 (case 5). The same field selects the per-language text slot vm+0x334+lang*4 used by SE_ReadText / SE_ExistsText.

name: SE_FreeText
summary: Frees all loaded text pages of all languages.
semantics: Frees ALL loaded script text pages of ALL languages: Script::FreeAllTextPages(vm) walks the 999 per-language slots vm+0x334.., removes every page entry, destroys string cells, frees the memory and zeroes the slot. Afterwards SE_ReadText / SE_ExistsText find nothing until texts are loaded again (SE_XMLImportText, SE_LoadText, SE_LoadAllTexts). Always returns int 0. Side effect on engine/VM text tables.
notes: Handler 0x4ae6a4 (case 6). Emulator: clear the text database, return 0.

name: SE_StringLen
summary: Returns the length of a string in bytes (0 for a non-string).
semantics: arg1 via CellGetString (type 2 pool string or type 0xb heap string, else NULL). NULL -> 0. Otherwise strlen in BYTES (UTF-8 bytes, not characters; SE_StringNumChars is the char counter). Sync.

name: SE_StringNumChars
summary: Returns the number of characters of a UTF-8 text (continuation bytes and escape codes not counted).
semantics: Number of characters of s (not bytes) with the game's text convention: scan bytes; a byte with (b&0xC0)==0x80 (UTF-8 continuation) is not counted; a byte 0x1B (ESC) is not counted AND the byte after it is skipped too (colour/format escape pair); every other byte counts 1. Non-string arg1 (CellGetString NULL) -> 0. Empty string -> 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ac367. If the string ends in a lone 0x1B the scan steps past the terminating NUL (reads beyond the string; undefined). Only arg1 is read.

name: SE_StringNextCharPos
summary: Returns the byte offset of the next UTF-8 character start after a position.
semantics: UTF-8 aware 'next character start'. s = string of arg1 (CellGetString: cell tag 2 = pool string, tag 0xb = heap string; any other tag -> NULL). If s is NULL returns 0. pos = raw dword of arg2, compared UNSIGNED with strlen(s). If pos >= len (so any negative pos too) returns len. Else returns the smallest index j > pos with s[j]==0 or (s[j]&0xC0)!=0x80, i.e. the byte offset of the character that follows the one containing byte pos (scan starts at s[pos+1]). Result is always in (pos, len].
fl: same (in the FL database the helper 0x0050ba30 this case calls is misnamed Util::Utf8PrevCharOffset; it steps forward)
notes: Handler 0x4ac3b5 (case 9). Counterpart of SE_StringPrevCharPos. Termination guaranteed by the NUL.

name: SE_StringPrevCharPos
summary: Returns the byte offset of the UTF-8 character start before a position.
semantics: UTF-8 aware 'previous character start'. s NULL (non-string arg1) -> 0. Util::Utf8PrevCharOffset(s, pos): pos is taken UNSIGNED; if pos==0 return 0; len=strlen(s); if pos>len then pos=len (a negative pos therefore becomes len); i=pos; loop { i-=1; if i==0 return 0; if (s[i]&0xC0)!=0x80 return i; }. So it returns the start offset of the character that precedes byte position pos; for pos=1 (or when only continuation bytes precede) it returns 0.
fl: same (FL inlines the backward scan; the FL database name of the helper called by SE_StringNextCharPos is misleading)
notes: Handler 0x4ac41c (case 0xa), helper Util::Utf8PrevCharOffset 0x004ee6a0 (EDI=s, EDX=pos).

name: SE_StringReadChar
summary: Returns the byte at a position of a string (0 when out of range).
semantics: argc==1: returns the first byte of s (0 for ""). Otherwise pos = arg2 raw (signed): 0 <= pos < strlen(s) -> s[pos] as unsigned byte (UTF-8 bytes, not characters), else 0. No other checks. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
x3_src: differs: B162 (non-string s reads as "", answer 0)
bugs: AP 0x004ac23e (FL 0x004c8d71): a non-string s is NULL and is dereferenced (crash). Fixed in x3_src (B162).

name: SE_StringWriteChar
summary: Returns a copy of a string with one byte replaced.
semantics: Copies s (heap copy, strlen+1). argc==1: copy[0] = low byte of the cell AFTER the arguments (args[1], not passed). Otherwise: pos = args[2] raw; if 0 <= pos < strlen(s): copy[pos] = low byte of args[1] (ch); out of range -> unchanged copy. Returns the copy as a new string (s itself is not modified). Writing byte 0 truncates the result; writing into a UTF-8 sequence breaks it. Use the three-argument form only. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
bugs: AP 0x004ac29c (FL 0x004c8dd6; x3_src reproduces): the argument count test is off by one - the argc==1 branch writes args[1], which was not passed, and the two-argument form (s, ch) reads the position from args[2], which was not passed either (stale VM stack cell): with 2 args the write lands at an arbitrary position or nowhere. Also a non-string s was strlen(NULL) (fixed, B162).

name: SE_StringStr
summary: Returns the byte offset of the first occurrence of a substring (optionally from a start offset), or -1.
semantics: Either of arg1/arg2 not a string -> -1. If argc>2: start=arg3 (unsigned compare); if start >= strlen(hay) (so also any negative start) -> -1; argc<=2: start=0. Then CRT strstr(hay+start, needle): result = byte offset of the match from the START OF hay (not from start) or -1 if not found. Empty needle matches immediately, result = start. Case sensitive. Sync.
notes: Offsets are bytes.

name: SE_StringChr
summary: Returns the byte offset of the first occurrence of a byte in a string (optionally from a start offset), or -1.
semantics: arg1 not a string -> -1. If argc>2: start=arg3; start>=strlen (unsigned, negatives too) -> -1. Then CRT strchr(s+start, (char)ch): ch is truncated to its low byte; result = byte offset from the start of s, or -1. ch==0 (or ch&0xff==0) matches the terminator and returns strlen(s) (when start<strlen). Case sensitive. Sync.

name: SE_StringRChr
summary: Returns the byte offset of the last occurrence of a byte in a string, or -1.
semantics: Index (byte offset) of the LAST occurrence of byte ch (low byte of args[1].value, CRT strrchr semantics) in s, or -1 if absent. ch==0 returns strlen(s). Non-string s (CellGetString NULL) -> -1.

name: SE_StringSub
summary: Returns a substring by byte start and optional length ("" when out of range).
semantics: s not a string -> ''. n=strlen(s); start is compared UNSIGNED: start>=n (incl. negatives) -> ''. argc<3 -> s[start:]. argc>=3: len unsigned; if len>=n or start+len>=n -> s[start:] (negative len also gives the rest). Otherwise len bytes from start, but if len!=0 the length is extended forward while the byte at s[start+len] is a UTF-8 continuation byte (&0xC0==0x80), so a multibyte char is never cut; len==0 -> ''. Returns a new string cell. Sync.
notes: Result is built with SetCellStringDup(ptr,len) in the extended case, plain copy of the tail otherwise.

name: SE_StringToInt
summary: Parses a decimal integer from a string (atol); 0 for a non-string or garbage.
semantics: Only if arg1.type is 2 or 0xb: result = CRT atol(string) (leading whitespace, optional sign, decimal digits, stops at first non-digit; garbage -> 0; MSVC atol does not clamp, overflow wraps in 32 bits). Any other cell type (int, double, array...) -> 0. Sync.

name: SE_StringSplit
summary: Splits a string on a separator and returns an array of the pieces.
semantics: Splits s on every non-overlapping occurrence of sep (strstr, case-sensitive; scan restarts at match+len(sep)). Returns array of count+1 heap strings: pieces before each separator, then the remainder (so trailing separator gives a trailing empty string; empty s gives [""]; no match gives [s]). Separator pieces are not included. Empty sep: strstr(s,"") returns s every time -> the counting loop never ends (hang). Non-string s or sep: CellGetString returns NULL -> access violation (crash). Result via ResumeTaskWithCell (array copy).
x3_src: differs: bugs_fixed.md 7b4452b (empty separator no longer hangs)
bugs: AP 0x004ac731: an empty separator makes the counting loop endless - game hangs. Fixed in x3_src.
notes: strstr is Crt::Strstr 0x005108e0 (plain CRT). Pieces created with SetCellStringDup(ptr,len), last with ArraySetString.

name: SE_StringSubst
summary: Replaces every occurrence of a substring by another string.
semantics: If any of the three is not a string (CellGetString NULL): result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged (whatever type it was). If s does not contain find: result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged (same cell, pool-string stays type 2). Else: all non-overlapping occurrences left-to-right are replaced by repl (scanning resumes after each match, replaced text is not rescanned); result is a new heap string. Case sensitive.
x3_src: differs: B142 (buffer size in 64 bits) and bugs_fixed.md 7b4452b (empty search string no longer loops)
bugs: AP 0x004ac7da: an empty search string loops for ever writing past the heap buffer (0x004ac896); the size (R+1-F)*S overflows int32 for long strings (B142). Both fixed in x3_src.
notes: Empty 'find' makes strstr return s itself every time: the loop never advances, overflows the buffer / hangs (buffer = max(len(s), (len(repl)+1-len(find))*len(s))+1). Do not emulate; treat as undefined.

name: SE_SPrintf
summary: Formats a string with the script printf (%d %s %f %a %!N ...).
semantics: Result = new string = Script::FormatString(fmt, args[2..argc], nargs=argc-1) (computed twice: first for length, then filled). fmt not a string -> ''. Spec: %[!N][flags][width][.prec][h|l|L]conv. '%!N' (N one digit 0-9) selects explicit zero-based argument N (relative to the args after fmt) and does not advance the argument counter; otherwise args are consumed in order. flags: space(8) # + - 0. width/precision: digits or '*' (takes next arg: int cell value if type 1 else 0; negative width => left-justify). '.' alone => precision 0. conv: d i (signed), u x X o (unsigned; 'h' => 16 bit), integer value = arg.value ONLY if the cell type is 1 (int), else 0 (so a string/double/array arg prints 0; a missing arg (index>=nargs) prints 0). e E f F g G: double read ONLY if cell type is 0xe, else 0.0 (ints are NOT converted: %f of an int prints 0.0). c: char = low byte of int arg (type 1 else 0 -> a NUL byte). s: type 2 or 0xb string; any other type or missing arg -> literal '<invalid>'; precision truncates, width pads with spaces. a: debug dump of any cell (Script::ValueToDebugString with depth=maxelems=INT_MAX): int '%d', pool string 'text' in SINGLE quotes, heap string "text" in DOUBLE quotes, array {e1,e2,..} ({} if empty, lazy untouched arrays print {0,0,..}), table [k:v,k:v,..] in iteration order ([] if empty), double %g, object '<object N>' / '<object null>', function ref '[%06x]...', other '<type N>'; missing arg -> '[NULL]'. '%%' -> '%'. Unknown conversion char X -> the two characters '%X' are copied; a lone '%' at end of string -> '%'. Length modifier l/h/L accepted; 'l' only changes which path reads the int (same value). No locale; float formatting is the CRT style via BuildFloatFormat. Sync.
notes: Helpers: FormatString 0x004a6d80, FormatArgInt 0x004a6d10, FormatArgString 0x004a6d30, ValueToDebugString 0x004a94f0, BuildFloatFormat/FormatInteger not read in detail (assumed C printf semantics incl. flags). The result cell is type 0xb. Each arg is read at args+5*idx without regard for argc>nargs only via the idx<nargs check.

name: SE_VSPrintf
summary: Formats a string like SE_SPrintf, the arguments taken from an array.
semantics: Same format rules as SE_SPrintf (Script::FormatString: %d %s %f %a %!N etc.), with the argument cells = the elements of arg2 (count = ArrayGetSize(arg2)). Two passes (length, then fill) into a new string cell; allocation failure -> "". fmt not a string -> "". Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
x3_src: differs: B161 (non-array or untouched lazy array formats without arguments)
bugs: AP 0x004abb7d (FL 0x004c8787): arg2 is read as an array without a type check ([value+0x10] of any cell), and an untouched lazy array (SE_ArrayAlloc(n) never written) has no cell storage yet -> NULL read; a non-array arg2 reads garbage. Fixed in x3_src (B161).

name: SE_strcmp
summary: Case-sensitive string compare returning -1, 0 or 1.
semantics: If arg1 is not a string cell (type 2 or 0xb) -> -2; else if arg2 is not a string -> 2. Otherwise compares the bytes unsigned, left to right: first difference -> -1 (a<b) or 1 (a>b); equal -> 0. A prefix is smaller ("ab" < "abc"). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_stricmp
summary: Case-insensitive string compare (CRT _stricmp difference; -2/2 for non-strings).
semantics: If args[0] is not a string cell (type 2/0xb) returns -2; else if args[1] is not a string returns 2; otherwise returns CRT _stricmp(a,b): the difference lower(a[i])-lower(b[i]) at the first differing byte (ASCII A-Z folded, C locale), 0 if equal; NOT normalized to -1/0/1 (can be any int). Prefix: a shorter than b gives a negative number (0 - char).
notes: MSVC ___ascii_stricmp 0x00517a73: SUB EAX,ECX of lowered bytes. If the locale flag DAT_0057e27c is non-zero the locale-aware __stricmp_l is used instead (not normally the case).

name: SE_CTime
summary: Formats a time (default: now) as the C ctime() text without the newline.
semantics: argc==0: t = _time64(NULL) (host wall clock); else t = arg1 raw dword zero-extended to 64 bits (so negative values mean times after 2038). Result = _ctime64(&t) with the trailing newline removed, e.g. "Wed Jan 02 02:03:55 1980" (host local time zone, 24 chars). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_TimeString
summary: Formats a time (default: now) with strftime, at most 48 characters.
semantics: strftime(buf[0x31], fmt, localtime64(t)) -> string. If argc==1 uses the current time (_time64), otherwise t=args[1].value taken as unsigned 32-bit zero-extended to 64-bit. Local time zone of the host. Output limited to 48 chars: if the formatted result does not fit the CRT call fails (returns 0) and the buffer content is whatever the CRT left (probably empty string); buf[0x31] is forced to 0. localtime64 failure (NULL) or non-string fmt -> CRT invalid-parameter handling (likely crash).
bugs: AP 0x004ae502: a non-string format is strftime(NULL) - CRT invalid parameter ends the process. Fixed in x3_src (B162).
notes: Result via ResumeTaskWithString. Output depends on host clock/locale (C locale strftime). Emulator may substitute a fixed clock.

name: SE_ArrayAlloc
summary: Creates a new array of n elements (int 0, storage allocated lazily).
semantics: Result = SetCellArray(resultcell, n.value) (raw dword, type not checked): a new array of n elements, refcount 1. It is 'lazy': storage is not allocated until the first element access, and then EVERY element is initialised to int 0 (cell type 1, value 0). So all elements read as int 0 (never empty/NULL type 0). n==0 gives an empty array that behaves as size 0. n<0 (as signed): SetCellArray fails, result cell is left untouched = an empty cell (type 0), the task is resumed with that. Huge n: allocation failure => same as failure. Sync.
notes: Array object: +0 id, +4 refs, +8 size (stored as -n while lazy), +0xc capacity, +0x10 cells. Array cells hold refs (arrays/tables/strings are shared by CopyCell with refcount, not deep-copied; doubles (0xe) and int64 (0xd) are deep copied).

name: SE_ArraySize
summary: Returns the number of elements of an array (0 for a non-array).
semantics: ArrayGetSize(arg1): abs(size) if arg1.type==8 and the array pointer is non-NULL, else 0 (any non-array argument => 0, no error). Lazy arrays report their real element count. Sync.

name: SE_ArrayRead
summary: Returns element i of an array (0 if out of range or not an array).
semantics: ArrayGetElement(a, i): NULL when a is not an array, i < 0 or i >= size; a lazy array (SE_ArrayAlloc) gets its storage (all int 0) on first access. Result = CopyCell of the element: ints, strings and numbers by value, arrays and tables by reference (refcount +1, the same object). NULL -> int 0. Equivalent to the a[i] expression. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_ArrayWrite
summary: Stores a value into element i of an array (ignored if out of range).
semantics: ArraySetElement(a, i, v): not an array or i outside 0..size-1 -> nothing; otherwise the old element is released and v copied in (arrays/tables shared by reference). Does not grow the array (SE_ArrayResize/Append do). Returns int 0. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_ArrayCopy
summary: Copies the elements src[srcStart, srcEnd) into dst at dstStart (5th arg is an END index).
semantics: Copies src[srcStart .. end) into dst starting at dstStart. NOTE: 5th argument is an END INDEX in src, not a length. srcSize=ArraySize(src) (0 if not an array), dstSize=ArraySize(dst). If end<0 or end>srcSize then end=srcSize. Loop: while dstIdx<dstSize and srcIdx<end: dst[dstIdx]=copy of src[srcIdx] (ArraySetElement/CopyCell: reference types share the object, refcount+1); srcIdx++, dstIdx++. Loop is skipped entirely if dstStart>=dstSize. Out-of-range srcIdx (negative srcStart) gives NULL element -> CopyCell(NULL) stores int 0; negative dstIdx writes are silently ignored (ArraySetElement returns 0) while indexes keep advancing. Non-array dst or src: size 0 -> nothing copied. Always returns int 0.
notes: Native frame: handler reads args[k] (cell at args+5k, value dword at +1) WITHOUT checking argc unless stated, so a missing argument reads a stale stack cell. Dispatcher always returns 1 (never aborts the step). Arg layout from dis: dstStart=[args+6], srcStart=[args+0x10], end=[args+0x15]. Source and destination may be the same array (forward copy, overlapping not handled specially).

name: SE_ArrayClone
summary: Returns a shallow copy of an array (elements copied, contained arrays/tables shared).
semantics: n=ArraySize(a) (0 for non-array). Result = NEW array of n elements (lazy alloc), then for i=n-1 down to 0: dst[i]=CopyCell(src[i]) via ArrayGetElement (this MATERIALISES a lazy source: all elements become int 0). CopyCell semantics: ints/pool strings copied by value; heap strings, arrays, tables and objects are shared (refcount++), i.e. SHALLOW clone; doubles deep copied. Non-array arg => empty array. Sync.

name: SE_ArraySubClone
summary: Returns a new array with the elements [start, end) of an array.
semantics: start=arg2, end=arg3 (raw dwords; arg3 is read even if argc<3). n=ArraySize(a). If end<0 or end>n then end=n. If start<end: result = new array of (end-start) elements with dst[j]=CopyCell(src[start+j]) (shallow, same as ArrayClone; element at an out-of-range index, e.g. start<0, becomes int 0). If start>=end: result is the INT 0 (not an empty array!). Non-array arg: n=0 so end=0, start>=0 => int 0. Half-open range [start,end).

name: SE_ArrayInsert
summary: Inserts a copy of a value at an index of an array (index < 0 appends).
semantics: Inserts a copy of value (CopyCell) at position index, shifting later elements up; size+1. index<0 means append; index>size silently fails (nothing changes); index==size appends. If arr is not an array (or null) nothing happens. Always returns int 0 (the -1 from ArrayInsert is discarded). Capacity grows by 8 cells when full. Empty/lazy arrays are handled as normal arrays.
notes: Native frame: handler reads args[k] (cell at args+5k, value dword at +1) WITHOUT checking argc unless stated, so a missing argument reads a stale stack cell. Dispatcher always returns 1 (never aborts the step). Calls ArrayInsert(index=args[1].value, array=args[0], value=args+2).

name: SE_ArrayAppend
summary: Appends a copy of a value at the end of an array.
semantics: Script::ArrayInsert(-1, arg1, &arg2): appends a CopyCell of arg2 as the new last element (size+1). Non-array arg1 / NULL array: nothing happens. Always returns int 0 regardless of success. Capacity grows by 8 cells at a time; a lazy array just grows its virtual size and then materialises (all other elements int 0). Value is stored by CopyCell (heap objects shared by refcount). Sync.

name: SE_ArrayRemove
summary: Removes the element at an index from an array, shifting the rest down.
semantics: Script::ArrayRemove(arg1, arg2): removes the element at index (0-based): the element is destroyed, later elements shift down by one, size-1. Valid only for 0<=index<size; out of range (incl. negative, index==size) or non-array: silently nothing. Removing the last remaining element frees the storage (size 0). Lazy array: size shrinks by one regardless of index (all elements are int 0). ALWAYS returns int 0 (ArrayRemove's own -1 / 0 is discarded). Sync.

name: SE_ArrayResize
summary: Grows (with int 0) or shrinks an array to n elements.
semantics: Script::ArrayResize(arg1, arg2): no-op if arg1 is not an array, array pointer NULL, or n<0 (signed). n==size: nothing. Grow: new cells are int 0 (type 1, value 0). Shrink: tail cells destroyed (refs released). n==0 frees storage (size 0). Lazy array: just sets its virtual size to n. Result is ALWAYS int 0 (the handler jumps to the 'return 0' exit). Sync.

name: SE_ArrayFind
summary: Returns the index of the first element equal to a value (from an optional start), or -1.
semantics: Linear search from index start (start taken only if argc>2; negative/0 start -> 0) to size-1 for the first element equal to needle; returns its index or -1. Not an array -> size 0 -> -1; start>=size -> -1. Equality is Script::CellEquals(element, needle): int vs int by value; int vs double and double vs double numeric; string(2/0xb) vs string(2/0xb) byte-exact case-sensitive content compare; same-type arrays/tables/objects (8,9,0xa) by reference identity (pointer); any other mismatch of types falls to 'both falsy' test (CellIsTrue: 0, empty string pointer 0, null object, 0.0 are false): equal iff both are false. E.g. int 0 equals empty/zero double, int 5 vs string "5" is not equal. Same-type cells of other kinds (0,3,0xd,...) compare unequal. NULL element (out of range) is skipped.
notes: CellEquals 0x004a8a10. NOTE CellIsTrue returns true for string cells with non-zero offset/pointer, so an empty string is TRUE (it is a pointer).

name: SE_TableAlloc
summary: Creates a new empty table (hash map).
semantics: Result = SetCellNewTable: a new empty table (type 9), refcount 1, bucketCount=4, bucket array NULL until the first insert, count 0. Arguments ignored. Sync.
notes: Table object: +8 buckets ptr, +0xc bucket count (power of 2), +0x14 entry count. Node 0x10 bytes: +0 next, +4 key cell, +9 value cell.

name: SE_TableSize
summary: Returns the number of entries of a table (0 for a non-table).
semantics: TableCount(arg1): number of entries (table object +0x14) if arg1.type==9 with non-NULL object, else 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableNew
summary: Adds a value under a new automatic integer key and returns the key.
semantics: Appends value (CopyCell) under a fresh automatic integer key and returns that key. Uses the per-table counter (table+0x10, initial 1): counter+=1 (wraps to 1 after 0x7ffffffe), skipping values that already exist as INT keys; the first key issued by a fresh table is therefore 2. Returns 0 if t is not a table or no free key was found after a full wrap. Insertion via TableInsertAndGrow (rehash when count>=4*buckets).
notes: TableAppendNextKey 0x004aaae0. Key 0 is never returned, so 0 means failure.

name: SE_TableAdd
summary: Sets table[key] = value (or = key with two arguments), inserting or overwriting.
semantics: argc==2: table[key]=key (the value is the key cell itself). argc!=2 (3): table[key]=value. Insert-or-overwrite: Script::TableSet; existing key => value cell replaced via CopyCell (key kept), count unchanged; new key => node appended at the TAIL of its bucket chain, count+1. Returns int 1 if arg1 is a table with non-NULL object (even when overwriting), 0 otherwise (nothing done). KEY RULES: only int (type 1) and string (type 2/0xb, compared by content, case sensitive, pool and heap strings equal) keys are ever found again. Key of any other type (double, array, table, object, empty) hashes to bucket 0 and never compares equal, so every add of such a key appends a NEW unfindable duplicate node (TableExists/TableFind/TableRemove cannot reach it, but it is listed by TableKeys/TableNext). An int key never equals a string key (3 != '3'). Growth: after the insert, if count >= 4*bucketCount (i.e. bucketCount*4-1 < count) the table is rehashed to 2*bucketCount: old buckets are walked 0..n-1, each chain front to back, and each node is pushed at the HEAD of its new chain (so relative order inside a chain is reversed). Hash: int -> key & (buckets-1) (two's complement); string -> h=0; for each BYTE c (unsigned): h = c + 2*h (32-bit wrap); h & (buckets-1). Other types -> 0.
notes: Both Set (0x004a7630), Rehash (0x004a77e0), HashKey (0x004aabe0) read in full. Iteration order = ascending bucket index, then chain order.

name: SE_TableFind
summary: Returns table[key], or 0 when the key is absent.
semantics: Lookup. Script::TableFindValue(key=arg2 cell, table=arg1 cell): if arg1 is not a table (tag 9), has no buckets, or the key is absent -> returns int 0 (indistinguishable from a stored 0; SE_TableExists tells presence). Keys: only int (tag 1, matched by tag+value) and string (tags 2 and 0xB, matched by case-SENSITIVE byte content; pool and heap strings compare equal); any other key type finds nothing. On a hit the VALUE cell is copied into the result (CopyCell: arrays/tables/strings/objects shared by reference with refcount+1, doubles deep-copied) and returned.
notes: Handler 0x4ad539 (case 0x2a). Hash: int key = v & (n-1); string h = c + 2h.

name: SE_TableExists
summary: Returns 1 if a table has the key, else 0.
semantics: If arg1.type==9: 1 if TableFindEntry(table,key) finds a node (same key rules as TableAdd: only int and string keys can match), else 0. Non-table arg1 => 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableNext
summary: Iterates the keys of a table: the first key, or the key after a given one; 0 at the end.
semantics: Iterates keys. argc==1: start. argc>=2: prev = arg2 only if CellIsTrue(arg2), else start. CellIsTrue is false for int 0, empty cell, pool string with offset 0, NULL refs, double 0.0 (a heap string or non-zero int is true; an EMPTY heap string "" is still true because it tests the pointer) => prevkey of int 0 (or 0.0) means START again. TableNextEntry: if arg1 is not a table / object NULL / bucket array NULL (empty table) -> result int 0. Otherwise: find the node of prev (TableFindEntry); if prev==start or the key is NOT FOUND (removed, never existed, or of an unfindable type such as double/object) -> scan restarts at bucket 0 and returns the FIRST key again. If found: next = node->next in the same chain; else the first non-empty bucket with index > prev's bucket (bucket from hash of prev, with the current bucket count). End of table -> int 0. Result = CopyCell of the next KEY cell (int or string key). => If the script removes the key it is currently standing on (the prevkey) before calling TableNext, iteration RESTARTS from the beginning (infinite loop risk); removing other keys is safe; inserting during iteration may rehash and reorder (rehash happens when count reaches 4*buckets). ORDER: buckets ascending (bucket index = hash & (n-1), n=4 initially, doubling), chain order inside a bucket = insertion order (tail append) unless the table was rehashed (chains reversed per rehash relative to old traversal order, see SE_TableAdd). Int keys 0..k in a fresh table therefore iterate in an interleaved order (bucket 0: 0,4,8..; bucket 1: 1,5,..), NOT insertion order. Sync.
notes: TableNextEntry 0x004aace0, CellIsTrue 0x004a8970, TableFindEntry 0x004aa9f0, TableHashKey 0x004aabe0. Verified in dis (CMP argc,1; LEA ESI,[EDI+5]; CALL CellIsTrue).

name: SE_TableRemove
summary: Removes a key from a table and returns its value (0 if absent).
semantics: TableFindValue(table,key): if arg1 is not a table or the key is absent (only int/string keys findable) -> result int 0 and nothing is changed. If present: result = CopyCell of the stored VALUE cell (the value that was removed, NOT a 1/0 flag), then the node is unlinked from its chain, key and value cells destroyed, count-1. Bucket array is never shrunk. NOTE the result is indistinguishable from 'absent' when the stored value was int 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableKeys
summary: Returns an array of the keys of a table in iteration order.
semantics: n=TableCount(arg1) (0 for non-table). Result = new array of n (lazy alloc) filled with the keys in TableNext iteration order (starting at the beginning, each step TableNextEntry(prevkey)), each key CopyCell'd. Because each step re-finds the previous key by lookup, unfindable key types (double/object/array duplicates) make the walk restart at the first key. Non-table or empty => empty array. Sync.

name: SE_TableData
summary: Returns an array of the values of a table in iteration order.
semantics: Returns an array of the table's VALUES (copies) in iteration order, length = number of entries (empty array if t is not a table or is empty). Element i is the value of the i-th key as returned by SE_TableKeys.
notes: Iteration order as described for SE_TableClone.

name: SE_TableRandomKey
summary: Returns the key of a random entry of a table (0 if empty).
semantics: Returns a copy of the key of a uniformly chosen entry: n=TableCount(t); if n<=0 (or not a table) returns int 0. Else i=rand()*n/32768 (Math::RandScaled, CRT rand, 0..n-1) and returns the i-th (0-based) key in table iteration order (key cell copy: int or string). Returns int 0 if iteration yields nothing.
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md
notes: RandScaled 0x004ee1c0 = (int64)n*rand()/0x8000 (truncating). Uses CRT rand() state (shared with TiScheduleDelay jitter etc.).

name: SE_TableNumberedKey
summary: Returns the key of the n-th entry of a table in iteration order (0 if out of range).
semantics: Returns a copy of the key of the n-th entry (0-based) in iteration order, if t is a table with count>0 and 0<=n<count; otherwise int 0. Iteration order = ascending bucket index, chain order within a bucket (see SE_TableClone notes).
notes: O(n) walk with TableNextEntry.

name: SE_TableClone
summary: Returns a new table with the same entries (values shallow-copied).
semantics: Returns a NEW table (SetCellNewTable on the task result: 4 buckets, auto-key counter=1, fresh id) filled by walking t in its iteration order (TableNextEntry from NULL) and inserting each (key,value copy) with TableInsertAndGrow (append at chain tail, rehash x2 when count>=4*buckets). If the argument is not a table (or empty) returns an empty new table. Values are copied with CopyCell (nested arrays/tables/strings shared by reference, not deep-cloned). The auto-key counter of the clone is NOT copied (restarts at 1). Iteration order of the clone can differ from the source (insertion history differs, rehash reverses chains).
notes: Result is written straight into task->result then ResumeTask. Hash/iteration details: bucket index = int key & (n-1); string key h=c+2*h over bytes then &(n-1); other key types bucket 0 (TableSet never matches them, so duplicates are appended). TableSet appends new nodes at the TAIL of the chain; TableRehash relinks every node at the HEAD of its new chain (walking old buckets 0..n-1, old chain order), so chains get reversed on each rehash. Iteration = buckets ascending, chain order. Grow condition after insert: count > 4*buckets-1.

name: SE_TableClear
summary: Removes all entries of a table in place.
semantics: In-place clear. If arg1 cell tag is 9 (table) and the table object pointer is non-NULL: destroys key and value cells of every node (releasing refcounts of contained arrays/tables/strings), frees all nodes and the bucket array, then resets the header: buckets=NULL (+8), auto-key counter (+0x10)=1, bucket count (+0xc)=4, entry count (+0x14)=0. The table object and all references to it stay valid and are now empty. Any other arg type: silent no-op. Always returns int 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ad806 (case 0x33) -> Script::TableClear 0x004a83e0. The counter at +0x10 is the 'next numbered key' used by TableAppendNextKey, so numbering restarts at 1 after a clear.

name: SE_GetTaskID
summary: Returns the id of the calling task.
semantics: Result = id of the calling task (task+8). Sync.

name: SE_TaskExists
summary: Returns 1 if a task with the id exists.
semantics: Returns 1 if a task with id = raw dword of arg1 exists in the VM task table (vm[0], hash map keyed by task id: bucket = id & (nBuckets-1), node key at +4, task pointer at +8), else 0. The calling task itself exists. Arg type is not checked. Implemented with the generic id->pointer lookup that Ghidra names Cockpit::FindByHandle.
notes: Handler 0x4abfa9 (case 0x35). Result normalised to 0/1 (NEG/SBB/NEG). Task ids come from SE_GetTaskID / task start natives; ids of finished tasks disappear from the map.

name: SE_KillTask
summary: Kills the task with the given id (immediately).
semantics: FreeTaskById(arg1.value): looks the id up in the VM task hash; if a task exists it is freed (killed) at once; unknown id => nothing. Then the caller's own id is looked up again (the helper named Cockpit::FindByHandle is really the task-by-id lookup, also used by SE_TaskExists): if the calling task still exists it is resumed with int 0; if the caller killed ITSELF, no result is delivered and the dispatcher returns 0 (step aborted, scheduler yields to the next frame; the task is gone). Normal result: int 0. Arg type is not checked.
notes: FreeTaskById 0x004a2590, handler dis 0x004abfce.

name: SE_ObjectExists
summary: Returns 1 if an object reference/id refers to a live script object.
semantics: CellIsValidObject(arg1): if type 0xa (object ref): 1 iff the ref pointer is non-NULL and its object context pointer (+8) is non-NULL (object not destroyed), else 0. If type 1 (int): non-zero value => ResolveObjectContext(id) != 0 -> 1/0 (negative ids look up script-created objects, non-negative ids static class table); int 0 => 0. Any other type => 0. Sync.

name: SE_ObjectFunctionExists
summary: Returns 1 if an object (by id) has a script method of the given name.
semantics: Returns 1 if the object with id objId (args[0].value is used as the id regardless of cell type) has a script method called name in its class or any parent class, else 0. Id resolution (ResolveObjectContext): id>=0 -> static class-record table lookup; id<0 -> script-created object hash keyed by (-id-1); unresolved id -> 0. Method search: name compared case-sensitively (binary search, byte compare) in each class's OWN method table (class+0x28 count / +0x2c rows), walking parent chain (class+0x14). Quirk: the loop only starts if the object's own class has the merged table pointer (+0x30) non-zero, and ends when the parent pointer is NULL. name not a string -> CellGetString NULL passed to the search (likely crash).
notes: ObjectHasMethod 0x0049f730, FindMethodByName 0x004b0740.

name: SE_GetClass
summary: Returns the class id of an object.
semantics: Returns the class id (first dword of the class record) of an object. If args[0] is type 0xa (object ref): uses the object directly (returns 0 if its class pointer obj+8 is NULL). Otherwise args[0].value is treated as an object id and resolved with ResolveObjectContext (id>=0 static class records, id<0 dynamic objects); unresolved -> 0.
notes: Dispatcher default path returns int 0.

name: SE_IsClass
summary: Returns 1 if an object is of a class (or a subclass of it).
semantics: If CellIsTrue(arg1) is false -> 0. ctx = arg1.value if arg1.type==0xa else ResolveObjectContext(arg1.value) (so an int, or even a string cell, is treated as an object id). ctx==0 -> 0. Then if arg2.type==0xa (class reference): arg2's class pointer must be self-consistent (cls==cls->self) else 0; result 1 iff that class is in the object's class chain (the object's own class or any ancestor via parent pointer +0x14). Else (arg2 not a class ref): ObjectIsOfClass(ctx, arg2.value): 1 iff some class in the object's class chain (own or any ancestor) has id (class+0) == arg2.value. So subclass objects satisfy IsClass for their superclasses. Result 1/0. Sync.
notes: dis at 0x004ad879 read; ObjectIsOfClass 0x004aaff0.

name: SE_GetSuperClass
summary: Returns the parent class id of an object's class.
semantics: Parent class id of an object's class. If arg1 cell tag==0xA (object ref): obj = cell value; if obj+8 (class pointer) is 0 (dead/invalid object) -> return 0. Any other tag: ctx = Script::ResolveObjectContext(raw dword of the cell): value >= 0 -> static class-table lookup by CLASS ID (FindClassRecord), value < 0 -> script-created object hash lookup by -value-1; ctx==0 -> return 0. Then class = ctx[+8]; parent = class[+0x10]; returns 0 if parent == -1 (no parent), else parent (a class id as int). So it works for a plain int class id as well as for object refs.
notes: Handler 0x4ad8fc (case 0x3b). The class record field read is +0x10 (parent CLASS ID, -1 = none); SE_GetClass (0x39) returns class[+0]. script_vm.md lists the parent at +0x14, the code reads +0x10. A tag-0xA cell holding a NULL pointer would fault (the pointer itself is not checked).

name: SE_GetExprType
summary: Returns the type tag of a value (0 empty, 1 int, 2/11 string, 8 array, 9 table, 10 object, 14 double ...).
semantics: Result = the raw type byte of the argument cell: 0 empty, 1 int, 2 pool string (script string constant/text), 3 function/frame ref, 8 array, 9 table, 0xa object ref, 0xb heap string (runtime built string), 0xc/0xd int64 boxed, 0xe double, 0xf other. NO normalisation: a literal string constant is 2, the same text after SE_StringSub/concatenation is 0xb. Sync. (SE_IsString returns 1 for types 2 and 0xb.)

name: SE_IsString
summary: Returns 1 if the value is a string.
semantics: Returns 1 if args[0] is a string cell (type 2 pool string or type 0xb heap string), else 0.

name: SE_LinFunc
summary: Clamped linear interpolation of x between two points (integer).
semantics: Clamped linear interpolation, all 32-bit ints: args = (x0=arg1, x1=arg2, y0=arg3, y1=arg4, x=arg5) passed to ClampedLinearRamp(x, x1, y1, x0, y0). if x0==x1: (y0+y1)/2 (C trunc division). elif x<=x0: y0. elif x>=x1: y1. else if x<0x10000 (signed) and (x1-x0)<0x10000 (signed): (y0+y1)/2 + MulDiv(y1-y0, 2*x-x0-x1, 2*(x1-x0)) else (y0+y1)/2 + (int)(((int64)(y1-y0)*(int64)(x-(x1+x0)/2))/(int64)(x1-x0)). MulDiv = IDIV based a*b/c truncating toward zero, c==0 -> 0 (64/32-bit IDIV: quotient overflow of 32 bits would raise a divide exception). Sync.
notes: Argument order verified from the push sequence at 0x004ace96 (ESI=arg3 pushed first, EDX=arg1 second; EAX=arg2, EDI=arg4, ECX=arg5). Note (x1+x0)/2 and 2*x-x0-x1 use 32-bit wrapping arithmetic.

name: SE_SmoothInterpolate
summary: Logistic S-curve interpolation of x from an input range onto an output range.
semantics: Logistic S-curve mapping; args a1..a5 = inLo, inHi, outLo, outHi, x (x is the LAST arg here). t = (x-inLo)/(inHi-inLo) (floating, not clamped; inHi==inLo -> inf/NaN); result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) / (1 + exp(-15*(t-0.5))) ) with the constants 0.5 and -15.0 stored as float32; x87 extended precision; Ftol truncates toward zero; NaN -> 0x80000000. Not normalised: at t=0 it gives outLo+d*0.00055, at t=1 outLo+d*0.99945 (never exactly the end values); outside [inLo,inHi] it keeps flattening, no clamp.
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Handler 0x4ace68 -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntSigmoid 0x004a5f50. (The clamped linear SE_LinFunc 0x3e takes x0,x1,y0,y1,x.)

name: SE_LogFunc
summary: Logarithmic interpolation of x in a range onto an output range.
semantics: Logarithmic interpolation. 5 args read as raw dwords (no type/argc check): x=a1, lo=a2, hi=a3, outLo=a4, outHi=a5. x is clamped to [lo,hi] (if x<lo x=lo; then if x>hi x=hi; signed). Result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) * ln(x/lo) / ln(hi/lo) ) in x87 extended precision (FYL2X*ln2); (outHi-outLo) is an int32 subtraction (wraps). Ftol truncates toward zero (double -> CVTTSD2SI); NaN/inf/overflow (lo=0, lo<0, lo==hi giving 0/0 ...) give 0x80000000 (-2147483648). x<=lo -> outLo, x>=hi -> outHi.
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Handler 0x4ace0e -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntLog 0x004a5e70 (EDX=outHi). Python doubles can differ from x87 80-bit only at exact integer boundaries.

name: SE_ExpFunc
summary: Exponential interpolation of x in a range onto an output range.
semantics: Exponential interpolation, args as SE_LogFunc: x=a1, lo=a2, hi=a3, outLo=a4, outHi=a5. x clamped to [lo,hi]. Result = Ftol( outLo + (outHi-outLo) * exp(x/lo) / exp(hi/lo) ) (x87 f2xm1/fscale, extended precision). The exponents are x/lo and hi/lo (NOT (x-lo)/...): at x==hi the result is outHi exactly, at x==lo it is outLo+d*exp(1)/exp(hi/lo), not outLo. Ftol truncates toward zero; lo==0 or overflow -> 0x80000000.
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Handler 0x4ace3b -> Script::NativeInterpolateIntExp 0x004a5ed0. No arg checks.

name: SE_LinFuncSum
args: x0:int, x1:int, y0:int, y1:int, xa:int, xb:int
summary: Sum of a clamped linear ramp over an integer range.
semantics: Trapezoid sum of the clamped linear ramp over an integer range. Ramp(x) = Math::ClampedLinearRamp with line (x0,y0)-(x1,y1): if x0==x1 -> (y0+y1)/2 (truncating toward zero); elif x<=x0 -> y0; elif x>=x1 -> y1; else mid=(y0+y1)/2 (trunc toward zero) plus: if x<0x10000 and (x1-x0)<0x10000: MulDiv(y1-y0, 2x-x0-x1, 2(x1-x0)) else (int32)(((int64)(y1-y0) * (x - (x0+x1)/2)) / (x1-x0)) ((x0+x1)/2 truncates toward zero; 64/32 IDIV, overflow traps). MulDiv(a,b,c) = 0 if c==0 else (int32)((int64)a*b/c) truncated toward zero. Result = ((Ramp(xa) + Ramp(xb)) * (xb - xa + 1)) / 2 with 32-bit wrap and the final /2 truncating toward zero. Args a1..a6 = x0,x1,y0,y1,xa,xb; no ordering check (xb<xa gives zero/negative counts).
notes: Handler 0x4acec4 -> Script::NativeClampedRampSum 0x004a5fb0 + Math::ClampedLinearRamp 0x0042fb20. Arg mapping verified in the disassembly: ramp calls use x0=a1, x1=a2, y0=a3, y1=a4; first x=a5, second x=a6. All ints, no type checks.

name: SE_CubicPoly
args: a1:int, a2:int, a3:int, a4:int, a5:int, a6:int, x:int
summary: Odd cubic polynomial of a clamped offset around a centre.
semantics: Odd cubic around a centre; 7 int args a1..a7 (a7 = x). t = min(max(x - a1, -a1), a1) (first the lower clamp against -a1, then the upper against a1); r = a6/a5 (floating); c = (a4 - r*a3) / a3^3 (floating); result = Ftol( a2 + r*t + c*t^3 ) in x87 extended precision (truncation toward zero). a5==0 or a3==0 -> inf/NaN -> 0x80000000. No type/argc checks. The curve passes through a2 at t=0 with slope r and equals a2+a4 at t=a3 (as written: a2 + r*a3 + c*a3^3 = a2 + a4).
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Handler 0x4acef4 -> Script::NativeCubicPoly 0x004a6010 (x in ECX, a1..a6 on the stack). Formula derived instruction by instruction (FDIVRP, FCOM clamp pair); note x and the clamp centre share a1.

name: SE_GGT
summary: Greatest common divisor (German GGT) of two positive ints.
semantics: Subtractive Euclid on the raw dwords: while a != b { if a < b (signed) b -= a else a -= b }; returns a. a == b returns at once. Only positive inputs terminate: 0 or a negative input loops forever inside the native (the game hangs; no yield). Large coprime values take O(max) iterations. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
x3_src: differs: fixed (bugs_fixed.md, commit 7b4452b): Euclid with modulo on absolute values; gcd(a,0) = |a|, gcd(0,0) = 0
bugs: AP 0x004acf29..0x004acf36 (FL 0x004c9aaa): SE_GGT(a,0), SE_GGT(0,b) or a negative argument never terminate - the game freezes. Fixed in x3_src (bugs_fixed.md "SE_GGT/SE_KGV with 0 and negatives").

name: SE_KGV
summary: Least common multiple (German KGV) of two positive ints.
semantics: Least common multiple (German KGV) = (a / gcd) * b with 32-bit wrap (signed IDIV/IMUL, low 32 bits), where gcd comes from SUBTRACTIVE Euclid: while a!=b { if a>b a-=b else b-=a }. a==b returns b. ZERO or NEGATIVE inputs never terminate (e.g. a=0,b=5: b-=0 forever; a<0 makes b grow) -> the game hangs inside the native (no scheduler yield). Large coprime values are slow (O(max) iterations).
x3_src: differs: bugs_fixed.md 7b4452b (zero/negative inputs answer 0 / use |a|,|b|, no endless loop or division by zero)
bugs: AP 0x004acf54: zero or negative input loops for ever (0x004acf74 area); KGV(0,0) divides by zero. Fixed in x3_src.
notes: Handler 0x4acf54 (case 0x45). SE_GGT (0x44) is the same loop returning the gcd. Emulator should treat a<=0 or b<=0 as an infinite loop error.

name: SE_Distance3
summary: Returns the integer length of the vector (x, y, z).
semantics: Returns trunc(sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)) computed in floating point: each int is converted to float32 (precision loss above 2^24), squares/sum done in x87 extended precision then stored as float32, then FSQRT, then Crt::Ftol truncation toward zero. Takes the three args by value (args[0..2]).
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Math::VecLengthToInt 0x0049c880, SqrtF 0x00412440. For |components| < 2^24 result equals floor(sqrt(sum)) up to float32 rounding of the sum.

name: SE_DistanceA3
summary: Returns the integer distance between a point array [x,y,z] and a point (x, y, z).
semantics: Euclidean distance between the point in array arg1 and the point (a2,a3,a4). Elements 0,1,2 of arg1 are fetched with ArrayGetElement (lazy arrays are materialised with int 0); if arg1 is not an array or has fewer than 3 elements -> returns int 0. Element values and a2..a4 are raw dwords (no type check). dx=A[0]-a2, dy=A[1]-a3, dz=A[2]-a4 (int32 wrapping subtraction), each converted to float32 (FSTP float: rounded to a 24-bit mantissa for |d|>2^24); the squares and sum are evaluated in x87 extended precision, the sum goes into FSQRT as a float; result = Ftol(sqrt(...)) truncated toward zero (floor for non-negative).
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Handler 0x4acfbf (case 0x47) -> Math::VecLengthToInt 0x0049c880 -> Math::SqrtF (FLD float; FSQRT). SE_Distance3 (0x46) is the same with 3 plain int args.

name: SE_DistanceAA
summary: Returns the integer distance between two points given as [x,y,z] arrays.
semantics: arg1 and arg2 are arrays of 3 int cells (x,y,z). All six ArrayGetElement(.,0..2) must be non-NULL (index in range, arrays valid, lazy arrays materialise to int 0) else result int 0. The int payload (cell+1) is read without checking the cell type. dx=a0-b0, dy=a1-b1, dz=a2-b2 (32-bit wrapping int subtraction). Result = VecLengthToInt(float(dx),float(dy),float(dz)) = (int)sqrt(float32(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz)): x87 evaluation, the sum is stored as a 32-bit FLOAT before FSQRT, then truncation toward zero (Crt::Ftol). Sync.
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Float32 precision limits: exact for results < ~4000; larger distances can differ by 1 from an exact integer sqrt. Emulate with float32 rounding of the converted inputs' squares sum.

name: SE_IsPosInRangeA
summary: Returns 1 if a point [x,y,z] lies inside any sphere of a (centre, radius) pair array.
semantics: Is the point arg1=[x,y,z] inside any sphere of arg2? arg2 is a flat array of pairs: element 2i = array[3] {cx,cy,cz} (int cells), element 2i+1 = radius (int). If arg1 is not an array with 3 elements -> 0. maxPairs = arg3 raw dword if argc>2 else -1 (all). n = array size of arg2 (abs of the stored size, 0 if not an array); if maxPairs>=0 and 2*maxPairs < n then n = 2*maxPairs. Loop i=0,2,4.. while i<n: element i must be an array (tag 8) with 3 usable sub-elements, else the pair is skipped; dist = Ftol(sqrt((x-cx)^2+(y-cy)^2+(z-cz)^2)) (int32 differences, converted by FILD, squares and sum in x87 extended precision, the sum rounded to float32 before FSQRT, Ftol truncates); hit if dist <= radius (signed int compare, radius = raw dword of element i+1). Returns 1 on the first hit, 0 if none.
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
bugs: AP 0x004af930: the radius element of the last pair is read without a NULL check (odd-length array crashes); x3_src reproduces (src/script/script.cpp:2966), not in bugs.md.
notes: Handler 0x4ad11d (case 0x49) -> Script::PointInAnySphere 0x004af930 (ECX=maxPairs). Radius element i+1 is dereferenced without a NULL check: an odd-length array whose last element is a valid centre array crashes. The compare uses the TRUNCATED distance (a point at distance radius+0.9 counts as inside).

name: SE_IsPosInRange3
args: x:int, y:int, z:int, spheres:array | x,y,z,spheres, maxPairs:int
summary: Is the point (x,y,z) inside any sphere of a (centre, radius) pair array.
semantics: Same test as SE_IsPosInRangeA but the point is given as three ints: Script::PointInAnySphere(maxPairs = arg5 if argc >= 5 else -1, x, y, z, spheres = arg4). spheres is a flat array: element 2i = array[3] {cx,cy,cz}, element 2i+1 = radius int; maxPairs >= 0 limits the pairs examined. A pair whose centre is not a 3-element array is skipped. Hit when the truncated distance (float sqrt) <= radius; returns 1 at the first hit, else 0. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
bugs: AP 0x004af930 (PointInAnySphere, shared with SE_IsPosInRangeA): the radius element 2i+1 is read without a NULL check - an odd-length array whose last element is a valid centre crashes; x3_src reproduces it (src/script/script.cpp:2966, radius->rawBits() without a check; not in bugs.md).

name: SE_CompressRangeData
summary: Removes spheres contained in other spheres from a (centre, radius) pair array in place; returns the pairs left.
semantics: In-place removal of spheres contained in other spheres from the flat pair array arg1 (element 2i = array[3] centre {x,y,z}, element 2i+1 = radius). maxPairs = arg2 raw dword if argc>1 else -1. n = min(arraySize/2, maxPairs) (maxPairs<0 or too large -> arraySize/2). If n<2 returns n and leaves the array untouched. Otherwise copies the n pairs into a temp table (radius,x,y,z); an element 2i that is not an array tag 8 or lacks three elements makes the native return 0 with the array untouched. Then for i=0..n-2: if r[i]>0, for j=i+1..n-1 with r[j]>0: d = Ftol(sqrt(float-cast squared centre differences)); if r[i]+d <= r[j] then r[i]=0 and break (sphere i lies inside j); else if r[j]+d <= r[i] then r[j]=0. The surviving pairs (temp radius > 0, so spheres with radius <= 0 are dropped as well) are compacted to the front of the script array in original order by copying the centre-array cell and radius cell (ArraySetElement). The array SIZE IS NOT REDUCED: slots after the compacted part keep their old values. Returns the number of surviving pairs.
notes: Handler 0x4ad1c8 (case 0x4b) -> Script::ArrayMergeContainedSpheres 0x004afbb0. Distance handling as SE_IsPosInRangeA. The radius cell at 2i+1 is read without a NULL check (crash if the length is odd).

name: SE_MulFix
summary: 16.16 fixed-point multiply with rounding.
semantics: 16.16 fixed multiply: ((int64)a*(int64)b + 0x8000) >> 16 (arithmetic shift of the signed 64-bit sum), low 32 bits returned as signed int (IMUL; ADD 0x8000; ADC; SHRD 16). Rounds half up. Overflow wraps in 32 bits. Sync.

name: SE_DivFix
summary: 16.16 fixed-point divide (0 for divisor 0).
semantics: 16.16 fixed divide: b==0 -> 0. Else ((int64)a<<16) / b with a 64-bit IDIV (EDX:EAX / ECX), truncating toward zero, remainder dropped (no rounding). If the quotient does not fit in 32 bits (|a/b| >= 32768.0 in 16.16, i.e. |(a<<16)/b| >= 2^31) the CPU raises #DE (integer divide exception) - the exe does not guard it; the emulator should treat it as a crash. Sync.
x3_src: differs: a quotient that does not fit 32 bits wraps (fixDivWrapOrZero) instead of the #DE crash; bugs.md KC-natives list "SE_DivFix" (still listed as open there)
bugs: AP 0x004ad243: IDIV without overflow check - a 16.16 quotient beyond 32 bits raises #DE (game crash). x3_src wraps.

name: SE_MulDivFix
summary: Returns a*b/c with a 64-bit intermediate product (0 for c = 0).
semantics: Math::MulDiv(a,b,c): c==0 -> 0. Else (int)(((int64)a*(int64)b)/c) via IMUL then IDIV ECX (64/32): truncates toward zero; if the quotient exceeds 32 bits the CPU raises #DE (unguarded). Pure integer: no 16.16 scaling is applied despite the name. Sync.
bugs: AP 0x004ad28b (Math::MulDiv): a quotient beyond 32 bits raises #DE (crash); x3_src mulDiv behaviour for that case not checked.

name: SE_Sqrt
summary: Integer square root (floor); 0 for negative input.
semantics: Integer square root, floor(sqrt(n)), computed with the classic bit-by-bit algorithm (bit starts 0x40000000, signed compares). n==0 -> 0; negative n -> 0. Result for 0<=n<=2^31-1 is exactly floor(sqrt(n)).
fl: same (FL calls the same bit-by-bit routine out of line, 0x00432aa0)

name: SE_Sin
summary: Fixed-point sine of a binary angle (16.16 result, table based).
semantics: Fixed-point sine. angle is a 16-bit binary angle (a = angle & 0xffff, 65536 = full turn). Returns 16.16 value (-65536..65536) from the quarter-wave table T[k] (k=0..0x4000), T[k]=Ftol(sin(k*9.58738019107841e-05)*65536.0) (truncate toward zero; the angle step is float32(2*pi/65536) widened to double): a<=0x4000: T[a]; a<=0x8000: T[0x8000-a]; a<=0xC000: -T[a-0x8000]; else -T[0x10000-a]. So sin(0)=0, sin(0x4000)=65536, sin(0x8000)=0, sin(0xC000)=-65536.
notes: Table Math::g_SinCosTable 0x005b6998 is filled at startup by Math::BuildAsinTable 0x004f0110 (call from Init::EngineConfigInit). Emulator should rebuild the table with the same formula (x87 FSIN at extended precision; tiny last-digit differences are possible).

name: SE_Cos
summary: Fixed-point cosine of a binary angle (16.16 result, table based).
semantics: Fixed-point cosine, same scale/table as SE_Sin: a = angle & 0xffff; a<=0x4000: T[0x4000-a]; a<=0x8000: -T[a-0x4000]; a<=0xC000: -T[0xC000-a]; else T[a-0xC000]. So cos(0)=65536, cos(0x4000)=0, cos(0x8000)=-65536, cos(0xC000)=0.
notes: See SE_Sin.

name: SE_Random
summary: Returns a random integer in [0, n-1] (0 for n <= 0).
semantics: n<1 (signed) -> 0. Else Math::RandScaled(n) = (int)(((int64)n * rand()) / 0x8000) using the MSVC CRT rand() (0..32767): result in [0, n-1]. Uses the shared CRT generator (seeded elsewhere by the engine); sequence cannot be reproduced exactly, emulator may use any uniform integer in [0,n-1]. Sync.
x3_src: differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md

name: SE_RandomLowNorm
summary: Returns a bell-shaped random number around 0 from n uniform samples of width 2m.
semantics: Random with a bell-shaped distribution: sum n samples s_i = (2a>0 ? RandScaled(2a) : 0) (each uniform in [0,2a-1], CRT rand()*2a/32768), avg = sum / n (signed integer division truncating toward zero; sum=0 if n<=0). If avg < a then avg = 2a - avg - 1 (mirror). Returns avg - a. For a>0 the result is in [0, a-1]: the mean of n uniforms concentrates around a, the mirror step folds the lower half onto the upper half, so after subtracting a the result clusters near 0 (more so for larger n). n==0 raises a division-by-zero exception (crash). a<=0: avg=0, result = -a.
x3_src: differs: bugs_fixed.md 7b4452b (n = 0 no longer divides by zero) and differs: random numbers come from per-task RNG channels (x3::rng, docs/arch/rng_split_r2.md), not the shared CRT rand(); same distribution, different sequence; not in bugs.md
bugs: AP 0x004ad49b: SE_RandomLowNorm(m, 0) divides by zero - #DE crash. Fixed in x3_src.
notes: Math::RandScaled 0x004ee1c0 = (int64)x*rand()/0x8000. Loop count n is read from args[1].value as signed; n<=0 skips the loop (but n==0 still divides).

name: SE_GetRotMatrixFromAngles
summary: Builds a 16.16 rotation matrix (3 row arrays) from three binary angles.
semantics: Returns a 3x3 matrix as array of 3 row arrays of 3 ints (16.16 fixed point). Angles are 16-bit binary angles (value & 0xffff, 65536 = full turn): theta = (v&0xffff)*1.5258789e-05f*6.2831855f (float32 constants widened). With sa,ca = sin,cos(theta(a)); sb,cb = theta(b); sg,cg = theta(g) and K=65536.0 (each entry Ftol-truncated toward zero): row0 = [K*(sg*sb*sa + cg*ca), K*sg*cb, K*(cg*sa - sg*sb*ca)]; row1 = [K*(cg*sb*sa - sg*ca), K*cg*cb, -K*(sg*sa + cg*sb*ca)]; row2 = [-K*sa*cb, K*sb, K*ca*cb]. (Some intermediate products sg*sb and sb*cg are rounded to float32 once.)
fl: same (FL is compiled with SSE2 float code instead of x87: last-bit rounding of float intermediates may differ, not compared)
notes: Math::AnglesToMatrix 0x004f0270 derived from x87 disassembly; matrix stored in 4-dword rows, handler packs the first 3 dwords of each row. Floating point order of operations may differ in the last ulp of the truncation; verify with a few sample angles if exactness at +-1 matters.

name: SE_GetAnglesFromRotMatrix
summary: Returns the three binary angles [a, b, c] of a 16.16 rotation matrix.
semantics: Inverse of SE_GetRotMatrixFromAngles(a,b,c) (M = Rc(c)Rb(b)Ra(a), 16.16, see SE_RotateVector). Reads the 3x3 matrix (3 row arrays of 3 ints, raw dwords; missing -> crash), calls Math::MatrixToEuler and returns a NEW array of 3 int cells [a, b, c], binary angles 0..0xFFFF (65536 = full turn). Table based (g_AsinTable with 65537 u16 entries indexed by the 16.16 value, cosine table, Math::AtanAngle), so results are table values; floats give +-1..2. With s=m[2][1] (=sin b) and cb=cos b: b = asin(s) (s>=0: table[s] in 0..0x4000; s<0: 0x10000-table[-s], i.e. 0xC000..0xFFFF); a = AtanAngle(FixedDivide(m[2][2],cb), -FixedDivide(m[2][0],cb)) (= atan2(-m20, m22)); c = AtanAngle(m[1][1]*65536/cb, m[0][1]*65536/cb) (= atan2(m01, m11)); if |s| > 0xE666 (near gimbal) a different, better conditioned formula for a is used. Gimbal s==+0x10000: b=0x4000, c=0, a=ftol(fpatan(m[0][2], m[0][0])) (minus 0x10000 if above 0xFFFF); s==-0x10000: b=-0x4000 (a NEGATIVE value), c=0, a=AtanAngle(m[0][0], m[0][2]).
bugs: AP 0x004ae8d4: missing rows/elements dereferenced as NULL (crash). Fixed in x3_src (B159).
notes: Handler 0x4ae8d4 (case 0x55) -> Math::MatrixToEuler 0x004f0640 (Ghidra's x87 parts unreliable; gimbal formulas uncertain). Matrix int index = row*4+col. Output array order = MatrixToEuler outputs (s04, eax, s08) = (a, b, c). An emulator without the tables can use atan2/asin in floats and round to the nearest binary angle; expect occasional off-by-one.

name: SE_GetAnglesFromVector
summary: Returns the yaw and pitch angles of a direction vector.
semantics: Math::DirectionToYawPitch on the three raw ints (any scale; only the direction matters) -> new array of 3 int cells: [0] = yaw (rotation about the vertical axis), [1] = pitch, [2] = 0 (never written). Binary angles 0..0xFFFF (65536 = full turn), the convention of SE_GetRotMatrixFromAngles / SE_RotateVector (a = yaw, b = pitch). The zero vector gives whatever DirectionToYawPitch returns for it (not traced). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_MatrixMultiplySelfRight
summary: In-place 3x3 product m1 := m2 x m1 (16.16).
semantics: In-place 3x3 matrix product: m1 := m2 x m1 (arg2 is the LEFT factor, arg1 the right factor and the destination). Each matrix is an array of 3 row arrays of 3 int cells (16.16 fixed point), read as raw dwords (missing rows/elements -> NULL deref crash). Math::MatMul: result[i][j] = sum_k R(m2[i][k]*m1[k][j]) with R(p) = (int32)(((int64)p + 0x8000) >> 16) applied per product (rounded) and the three rounded terms summed with 32-bit wrap. The 9 results are written back into the existing row arrays of arg1 via ArraySetInt (cells become int cells). arg2 is unchanged. Returns int 0.

name: SE_MatrixMultiplySelfLeft

semantics: Like SE_MatrixMultiplySelfRight but with the factors the other way: Math::MatMul(m1, m2) (AP 0x004aebf3: EAX = arg1 buffer, ECX = arg2 buffer), per product rounded 16.16 multiply ((p + 0x8000) >> 16), three terms summed with 32-bit wrap. The 9 results are written back into arg1's existing row arrays (ArraySetInt); arg2 unchanged. Rows/elements read as raw dwords. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_MatrixMultiply

semantics: Reads both matrices (3 row arrays of 3 ints, 16.16), Math::MatMul(m1, m2) (AP 0x004aed18: EAX = arg1, ECX = arg2) with rounded 16.16 products and wrapping sums, returns a NEW array of 3 new row arrays. Neither argument is modified. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

semantics: Math::RelativeRotationMatrix(m1, m2) (AP 0x004f1c50): out[r][c] = sum_k R(m1[r][k] * m2[c][k]), R = rounded 16.16 multiply, 32-bit wrapping sums. For rotation matrices transpose = inverse. Returns a NEW 3x3 array; arguments unchanged. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_RotateVector
summary: Rotates an int vector array in place by the matrix of two binary angles.
semantics: Rotates the integer vector in array arg1 IN PLACE and returns int 0. Reads vec[0..2] (ArrayGetElement raw dwords; missing elements -> NULL deref crash), angA=arg2, angB=arg3 (raw dwords; 16-bit binary angles: value&0xFFFF, 65536 = full turn). Builds M with Math::AnglesToMatrix(a=angA, b=angB, c=0), 16.16 fixed point: with ca=cos(2*pi*a/65536) etc., M = Rc(c)*Rb(b)*Ra(a), Ra=[[ca,0,sa],[0,1,0],[-sa,0,ca]], Rb=[[1,0,0],[0,cb,-sb],[0,sb,cb]], Rc=[[cc,sc,0],[-sc,cc,0],[0,0,1]] (row-vector convention); with c=0 that is M=[[ca,0,sa],[sa*sb,cb,-ca*sb],[-sa*cb,sb,ca*cb]]; each entry = Ftol(value*65536) (x87, truncation toward zero; sin/cos intermediates are spilled as float32 so +-1 LSB vs exact math). Then out = v x M: out[j] = sum_i R(v[i]*M[i][j]) where R(p) = (int32)(((int64)p + 0x8000) >> 16) per product (rounded 16.16 multiply) and the three terms are summed with 32-bit wrap. out[0..2] are written back with ArraySetInt (cells replaced by int cells). Plain ints work (result = v*M/65536 rounded).

The matrix formula was recovered by running the x87 listing of Math::AnglesToMatrix 0x004f0270 numerically and fitting; truncation order matters for bit-exact results.

name: SE_RotateVectorInv
summary: Rotates an int vector in place by the inverse (transpose) of the angle matrix.
semantics: Shares handler 0x004aeeec with SE_RotateVector: M = Math::AnglesToMatrix(angA, angB, 0) (16.16, binary angles), then Math::VecByMatrixRows: out[i] = sum_j R(M[i][j] * v[j]) (M times the column vector = v times M transposed, the inverse rotation), R = rounded 16.16 multiply, wrapping sums. vec elements are replaced by int cells; returns 0. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_ScriptComputeExpression
summary: Evaluates a postfix expression stored in a script array in place.
semantics: Evaluates a postfix (reverse Polish) expression IN PLACE in a script array; the native itself always returns int 0, the answer is left in buf[0] (type) and buf[1] (value). LAYOUT: buf is a flat array of 2*n cells; the array data pointer is read raw, so arg1 must be a materialised tag-8 array with >= 2n cells (no bounds/type checks). Pair k = (buf[2k], buf[2k+1]) = (T, V). arg2 = n = raw dword of arg2 = PAIR count, not cell count; n<=0 -> result (0,0). OPERAND pair: T != 15; T is the type code, taken from the dword value of cell buf[2k] (its cell tag is ignored); V is any value cell (int, double, string, object ref ...). OPERATOR pair: T == 15 (0xF) and the operator code is the dword value of buf[2k+1]. TYPE CODES used by the evaluator: 0 = none/false; 4 = number (int; value cell tag 1, or tag 0xE double); 5 = string (value cell tag 2 or 0xB); any code with bit 0x10000 set (e.g. 0x10006 ship, 0x10007 station, 0x10008 sector) = object (truthiness via CellIsValidObject); anything else (e.g. 10 race) is opaque. VARIABLES AND CONSTANTS ARE NOT LOOKED UP BY THIS NATIVE: the MSCI interpreter (x3story __runScript, command 104) has already resolved every operand to a (type,value) pair (local variable -> varTypes/varValues, 1 -> this-object, others via ScriptGetConst) and filled the buffer; the native only sees resolved values. EVALUATION: a static value stack of 100 cells (50 entries of two cells: type cell, value cell) at 0x00609440, with no overflow check. For each pair in order: operand -> push an entry (type cell := int cell with value T, value cell := CopyCell(V)); operator -> as follows. BINARY operators (code < 0x10000): if the stack is empty the operator is ignored; otherwise it pops B (top) and A (second; with a single entry on the stack A is stale memory below the stack) and writes the result into A's slot; typeA/typeB are the T codes. 0 '==', 1 '!=', 2 '>', 3 '<', 4 '>=', 5 '<=': if typeA==typeB: type 4 -> cmp = A.int - B.int (32-bit wrap); type 5 -> byte-wise unsigned strcmp (case-sensitive, sign only) if both value cells really are strings (tag 2/0xB), else cmp=1; any other equal type -> cmp = A.int - B.int only if both value cells have tag 1, else cmp=1, and for these other types ONLY == and != are supported (ordering ops give false). result = cmp==0 / !=0 / >0 / <0 / >=0 / <=0. If typeA != typeB: '==' gives false, '!=' gives true, ordering ops give false. 6 '&', 7 '|', 8 '^': need typeA==4 and typeB==4 else false; if both value cells have int tag 1 then A.val = A.val op B.val, otherwise A is left unchanged (type 4). 9 '&&': an operand is falsy if its type code is 0, type 4 with value 0, or an object type that is not a valid object; every other operand (nonzero int, string, valid object, opaque type) is truthy; result true iff both truthy. 10 '||': same truth rules, true iff either truthy. 0xB '+': both type 4 -> CellAdd in place (int add wraps, int+double promotes to double); otherwise the script method static __scriptOpAddString(typeA, valueA, typeB, valueB) is called synchronously (class id 0x2be, CallMethodStatic with the task id) and if it returns a string (tag 2/0xB) the result is (type 5, that string) else false (0,0). 0xC '-', 0xD '*': need both type 4 else false; CellSubtract / CellMultiply in place. 0xE '/', 0xF '%': need both type 4 and B's value dword != 0 else false; CellDivide / CellModulo in place (int division truncates toward zero). Any other code 0x10..0xFFFF -> false. BOOLEAN RESULTS: true = (type 4, int 1); false = (type 0, int 0) -- note false carries type code 0, not 4, so a following op sees typeA=0 (e.g. (a==b)+1 goes to __scriptOpAddString). UNARY operators (code has bit 0x10000; no pop, acts on the top entry, no empty-stack check): 0x10012 bitwise NOT: type 4 -> ~value if the value cell has tag 1 (else unchanged), other types -> (0,0). 0x10013 negate: type 4 -> CellNegate (int -v, double sign flip, object ref cell converted to its int id), other types -> (0,0). 0x10014 logical NOT: type 0 -> (4,1); type 4 with value 0 -> (4,1); an object type that is not a valid object -> (4,1); everything else (nonzero int, string, valid object, other types) -> (0,0). Any other unary code -> (0,0). RESULT: if the stack holds exactly one entry at the end, its type cell and value cell are CopyCell'ed into buf[0] and buf[1] (buf[0] becomes an int cell whose value is the result TYPE code: 4 number, 5 string, 0 false/none, 0x1000x object; buf[1] holds the result value cell: int, double, string or object ref); with 0 or >1 entries buf[0] = buf[1] = int 0. Cells after buf[1] keep their old contents. The two stack base cells are cleared; native return value int 0.
notes: Handler 0x4ab8ca (case 0x5d) -> Script::EvalExpression 0x004afe60 (args: vm, task, arg1 cell, arg2 cell). x3story caller: gExprTokenBuffer with instruction[2] pairs, result read from buffer[0], buffer[1] (type, value). Quirks: (1) ordering compare uses A-B in int32 so operands differing by >2^31 misorder; (2) string compares require real string cells; (3) no stack bounds checks (max 50 entries); (4) number type 4 with double cells goes through CellAdd/Subtract/... generic arithmetic; (5) logical NOT of a nonzero int yields type-0 false, of 0 yields (4,1). Decompile checked against the disassembly of the operand/operator dispatch.

name: SE_RegComp
summary: Compiles a regular expression and returns a handle (0 on error).
semantics: Compiles pattern with Regex::Compile (Henry Spencer regcomp) and returns a positive integer handle (auto id from Vm regex map +0x15f4, counter 1..0x7ffffffe), or int 0 if compilation fails (syntax error, NULL/non-string pattern, program too large >=0x7fff). Handles live until SE_RegFree.
notes: Counter start value (first handle presumably 1) not verified; HashMapAutoId 0x004efcc0 pre-increments.

name: SE_RegExec
summary: Runs a compiled regex on a string; 1 if it matches (groups kept for SE_RegSub).
semantics: Runs compiled regex re (from SE_RegComp) against s as an unanchored search (Henry Spencer regexec: tries each start position; ^ anchors at s start). Returns 1 if it matches anywhere, else 0. Unknown handle -> 0. Non-string s -> NULL -> 0. Exec also first rejects quickly using the regex's required literal if one was recorded. No capture results are exposed here (use the sibling Subst natives).
notes: Regex::Exec 0x004e6400; Henry Spencer v8 regexp variant (3-byte nodes, magic 0x9c). Syntax is the classic one: | ( ) * + ? . [ ] ^ $ and backslash escapes, no {n,m}, no non-greedy, case sensitive. Not fully verified against CompReg.

name: SE_RegSub
summary: Expands a template (& and \N) with the groups of the last SE_RegExec of a regex.
semantics: Expands a replacement template with the capture groups of the LAST SE_RegExec made with the same compiled regex. regexId = raw dword of arg1 = id returned by SE_RegComp (hash map vm+0x15f4). Unknown id -> returns the empty string. template = arg2 string (non-string -> NULL -> crash in CalcRegexReplaceLength). Henry Spencer regsub rules (Regex::Substitute): '&' = whole match (group 0); '\N' (backslash + digit 0-9) = capture group N; '\\' -> '\'; '\&' -> '&'; a backslash followed by any other char is output as a literal backslash and the next char is processed normally; all other chars are copied. An unset group (start or end pointer NULL) expands to nothing. The result goes into a buffer sized by CalcRegexReplaceLength (an upper bound) and is returned as a NEW heap string (tag 0xB). RegSub does no matching itself: if the regex never matched or the last match failed, all groups are NULL and the template is output with the group references removed. The group pointers (start at regexp+0, end at +0x28, 10 groups) point INTO the subject string passed to the last RegExec: if that string was freed or modified since, RegSub reads freed memory.

Pass 2 repeats the matching and writes Regex::Substitute(template) for each match one after the other. NOTE: the text between and around the matches is NOT copied - the result is only the expansions (e.g. subject "a1b2", regex "[0-9]", template "<&>" -> "<1><2>", not "a<1>b<2>"). No match -> "". Template rules as SE_RegSub (& and \N). After the call the regex groups describe the last failed search. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

Encoding: int (tag 1): <sval type="int" val="N"/>; strings (tags 2, 0xB): <sval type="string" val="text"/> (XML-escaped by libxml); double (tag 0xE): type="float" with val written by XmlSetValDouble; array (tag 8): type="array" size="N" with one child sval per element in order; table (tag 9): type="table" size="entry count" with children key1,value1,key2,value2,... in table iteration order (TableNextEntry = bucket order, not insertion order); every other tag (empty 0, object ref 0xA, function 3, ...): type="unknown" typeid="<tag byte>" (the value itself is lost). Returns the text as a new string; returns int 0 only if node allocation fails.

Root = first node of type element (xmlDocGetRootElement + sibling walk); none -> int 0. Otherwise Script::XmlToValue(root) builds a cell which is returned (ownership moved): the node must be an element named 'sval' (case-insens.), otherwise an EMPTY cell (tag 0) is returned. Attribute type selects: 'int' -> int cell from attr val (default 0); 'string' -> string cell from attr val; 'float' -> double cell (tag 0xE) from the val attribute; 'array' -> attr size=N (N<1 -> empty array of size 0), then every element child (the 'sval' name test inside the loop is applied to the PARENT node, so all element children are imported; a child that is not an sval gives an empty cell) is imported recursively and stored at index 0,1,2..; 'table' -> new table, attr size, element children alternate key, value, key, value... (TableInsertAndGrow); any other or missing type -> empty cell (tag 0). The libxml doc is freed.

Returns int 0 if the text is NULL/not a string, fails to parse, or has no element root. Element -> array [tagName:string, attrs, child1, child2, ...]. attrs = int 0 when the element has no attributes, otherwise a table keyed by attribute-name string; each value is an INT (atol) if the attribute text is an optional leading '-' followed by 1+ decimal digits only, otherwise a string (an empty value or just "-" stays a string). Children in document order: element children -> nested arrays (recursive); text nodes (xml type 3, including whitespace-only text between tags and entity-decoded text) -> strings; comments, CDATA (type 4), PIs are skipped. Attribute table is a normal script table (insert via TableSet with growth), so its key iteration order follows the hash rules.
