notes: Handler 0x4ae48c (case 0x89). SE_CTime (24, not in list) uses the same call but takes an optional time argument.

name: SE_QSortByName
summary: Sorts a range of an array by the string keys of a parallel key array (optionally descending).
semantics: Script::ArraySortRangeByString(a, keys, start, end, desc) with desc = (argc>=5 && arg5!=0). Silently does nothing unless both args are arrays (non-NULL) and 0<=start<end<size(a) AND end<size(keys) (end is INCLUSIVE; start==end, single element, is also a no-op). Otherwise: builds records for indices start..end of {key string = text of keys[i] (CellGetString: only string cells 2/0xb, any other type counts as ''), copy of a[i]}, sorts them with MSVC qsort using case-insensitive _stricmp ascending (descending when desc: operands swapped), NULL/non-string keys first (asc) / last (desc), and writes the sorted copies back into a[start..end]. keys[] is NOT reordered (pass the same array twice to sort strings in place). qsort is not stable: equal keys (case-insensitive) have unspecified relative order (MSVC qsort: quicksort, insertion sort for small partitions). Always returns int 0. Sync.
notes: Comparators 0x004aa630 (asc), 0x004aa660 (desc).

name: SE_QSortByInt
summary: Sorts a range of an array by the integer keys of a parallel key array (optionally descending).
semantics: Sorts arr[start..end] (inclusive) by the 32-bit payload (value dword at cell+1, whatever the cell type) of keys[start..end]; the elements of arr are permuted (cells moved, not copied); keys is NOT modified. Executed only if: both args are arrays, start>=0, start<end, end<ArraySize(arr) and end<ArraySize(keys) (sizes read from the raw array header, lazy arrays with negative size fail the test); otherwise silent no-op. desc=(argc>=5 && args[4].value!=0): non-zero -> descending (comparator b.key-a.key), zero/absent -> ascending (a.key-b.key). Comparators are plain 32-bit subtraction (overflow wraps) fed to CRT qsort -> NOT stable, order of equal keys unspecified. Always returns int 0.
notes: ArraySortRangeByInt 0x004aa820; comparators 0x004ab160 (asc) and 0x004aa690 (desc). Arg order from dis: array=args[0], keyArray=args[1], start=args[2], end=args[3].

name: SE_ToInt
summary: Converts a double (truncation) or a numeric string (atol) to an int; other types give 0.
semantics: Type conversion with a trap: double (type 0xe) -> truncated toward zero by Crt::Ftol (MSVC _ftol2_sse, AP 0x0052b5d0: with SSE2, i.e. on any real CPU, CVTTSD2SI at 0x0052b5e5, so a value outside the int32 range, NaN or inf gives 0x80000000; the x87 path at 0x0052b606 that keeps the low 32 bits of a 64-bit truncation runs only without SSE2); string (type 2 or 0xb) -> atol() (leading whitespace, optional sign, decimal digits, stop at first non-digit, 0 if none, overflow wraps); EVERYTHING ELSE INCLUDING int returns 0 (an int argument is NOT passed through).
fl: same (CVTTSD2SI at FL 0x004c987e: out of range, NaN or inf gives 0x80000000)
x3_src: differs: static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<int64_t>(d)) (native_dispatch.cpp seToInt) wraps for |d| in [2^31, 2^63) and gives 0 for NaN/inf, where AP and FL give 0x80000000
notes: Verified in dis: only compares tags 0xe, 2, 0xb; other tags jump to the 'push int 0' stub. Out of range: AP Crt::Ftol 0x0052b5d0 is _ftol2_sse; it tests the SSE2 flag [0x006619ec] and converts with CVTTSD2SI (0x80000000 out of range), like FL; the low-32-bit x87 path 0x0052b606 is only taken without SSE2.

name: SE_GetNum

semantics: Returns 1 when (vm.flags & 2) == 0 or (vm.flags & 4) != 0, else 0. The meaning of VM flags 0x2/0x4 was not traced (x3_src names them NO_NUM / NUM_OVERRIDE). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_CalcGalaxyEscortOffset
args: dx:int, dy:int, dz:int, offRight:int, offUp:int, offFwd:int
summary: Turns a formation offset (right, up, forward) in the leader's frame into a world offset vector.
semantics: dir = (dx,dy,dz); all zero -> int 0. fwd = NormalizeIntVec3(dir) (16.16); up = (0,1,0), or (0,0,-1) when |up.fwd| > 0.95 (0xf333); right = up x fwd, up = fwd x right (16.16 rounded cross products), both normalized. Then the result is computed IN PLACE in the offset vector o = (offRight, offUp, offFwd): o.x = right.x*o.x + up.x*o.y + fwd.x*o.z; o.y = right.y*o.x(NEW) + up.y*o.y + fwd.y*o.z; o.z = right.z*o.x(new) + up.z*o.y(new) + fwd.z*o.z (rounded 16.16 multiplies). Returns a new array [o.x, o.y, o.z]. Because of the in-place update y and z are not the true rotated components unless right.y/right.z are 0 (they are for a level leader: right = (fwd.z,0,-fwd.x)/n, so only z is affected). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
bugs: AP 0x004af1e7..0x004af240 (FL same): y and z use the already overwritten x (and y) - not a proper rotation. bugs.md open entry "SE_CalcGalaxyEscortOffset" (kept on purpose; x3_src reproduces, native_dispatch.cpp:1529).

name: SE_SetMaxOpCount
summary: Sets the per-slice operation limit of the VM and resets the counter.
semantics: Sets Vm+0x1604 (maximum operation count per task slice, initial 10,000,000) to args[0].value and resets the running counter Vm+0x1608 to 0. Returns int 0. (Switch case 0x8e, the neighbouring native, shares this same code.)
notes: Purpose of the field is inferred from the name; the interpreter uses it as an instruction budget. Emulator can ignore or implement as budget.

name: SE_SetDebugOutputFile

Nothing is opened here; the debug printers are compiled out, so in the release build the path has no visible use (no reader traced). name: SE_ConvertFormatString
summary: Expands {page,id} text references in a string (returns it unchanged when it has none).
semantics: arg1 not a string -> int 0. If the string contains no '{' character: result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged. Otherwise result = new string from Gui::ExpandTextReferences(s): every top-level balanced {page,id} (page and id decimal numbers; first char after '{' and after ',' must be a digit; atol each; page!=0) is replaced by the text GetText(page,id) of the CURRENT language, itself recursively expanded (nested {..} in that text). Any '{...}' that is not of that shape (no comma before the matching '}', non-digit start, page==0) is left in the output unchanged; an unbalanced '{' leaves the rest of the string as is. Missing text gives whatever Gui::GetText returns for a miss (the engine placeholder text). Sync.
notes: Handler only inspected via dis (strchr 0x7b then ExpandTextReferences 0x004ab320); ExpandTextReferences decompiled, brace matching logic summarised from that decompile (medium confidence on details of the literal-keep paths).

name: SE_ConvertTextString
summary: Unescapes a text-page style string (\n, \( etc.) into a new string.
semantics: Converts a text-page style string: duplicates arg1 (a non-string gives NULL; the following strlen(NULL) then crashes) and runs Script::UnescapeTextPageString IN PLACE on the copy; returns the copy as a new string. Rules (left to right over strlen bytes, with a 'skip' flag): '\n'->0x0A, '\b'->0x08, '\t'->0x09, '\r'->0x0D; '\' followed by octal digits 0-7 (any count, accumulated in 8 bits, stops at the first char outside '0'..'7') -> that byte; '\' followed by any other char -> that char literally (so '\(' gives '(' and '\\' gives '\'); a raw LF (0x0A) -> space; an unescaped '(' starts skip mode and an unescaped ')' ends it: everything (also escapes) inside is dropped and the parentheses themselves are not output; all other chars copied. QUIRK checked away (a terminator bug once assumed here was refuted 2026-10-29): the function writes no NUL terminator, but it returns the new length in EAX and the handler passes it on: ResumeTaskWithString 0x004a4860 pushes EAX as maxLen and ECX as the text for SetCellStringDup, which copies min(maxLen, strlen) bytes (Util::StrNDupReplace) and terminates. So the result is exactly the output bytes, cut at the first NUL byte (octal 000 or a lone trailing backslash give an early NUL); no tail of the input. Example: input of the 4 chars a, backslash, '(', b gives a, '(', b. Strings without backslash, parentheses or LF come out unchanged.
x3_src: differs: B162 (non-string converts the empty string)
bugs: AP 0x004acb1a: non-string argument -> strlen(NULL) crash. Fixed in x3_src (B162).
notes: Handler 0x4acb1a (case 0x93), Script::UnescapeTextPageString 0x004a4a60 (no store of 0 at the end; the length in EAX survives to ResumeTaskWithString at 0x004acb4f, whose register names in the database were swapped, which is how the tail was once assumed). The same function is used by text-page loading (ParsePageXml) with the stored length.

name: SE_StringMul
summary: Despite its name: XOR checksum of the bytes s[from..to-1].
semantics: argc == 3: x = XOR of the unsigned bytes s[i] for i = from .. to-1 (signed loop, no bounds check); other argc -> 0. Empty range -> 0. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
x3_src: differs: B160 (range clipped to the string; non-string -> 0)
bugs: AP 0x004ac672 / FL 0x004c9169: from/to are not checked against the string (reads outside it, negative from reads before it) and a non-string s is NULL. Fixed in x3_src (B160).

name: SE_VerifyData
summary: Verifies a signature of data with the Egosoft CryptoAPI key; 1 if valid.
semantics: Signature check through Windows CryptoAPI (provider 'Microsoft Base Cryptographic Provider v1.0', container 'X2EgosoftCSPContainer'). Needs argc==3 EXACTLY, arg1 a string with length>0, arg2 a string with length>0, arg3 an array (tag 8) with size>0; any violation returns int 0. The key blob = the low byte of every element of arg3 (n bytes). Script::VerifySignature: CryptImportKey(blob), MD5 (CALG_MD5 0x8003) of the strlen(arg1) bytes of arg1, base64-decode of arg2 (length must be a multiple of 4), CryptVerifySignatureA. SUCCESS: returns the base64 text of the MD5 digest (24 chars) as a string; any failure (bad key, bad signature, no provider) returns int 0. So the script gets either the digest string or 0. Otherwise pure computation (a CSP key container is created as a side effect).
notes: Handler 0x4af3b2 (case 0x95). The game does not refuse a script on failure (x3-mod doc script-signature-check.md). An emulator without the real key can return 0, or - to model 'signature valid' - base64(MD5(arg1)).

name: SE_SignData
summary: No-op stub: signs nothing, returns 0 (SE_SignGameStats is the working signer).
semantics: Release-build stub: arguments are ignored and int 0 is returned at once (AP shared stub 0x004abea2 with SE_SetProfiling/SE_SignData; FL shared stub 0x004cbdc6). Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_SignGameStats
summary: Signs a string with the game key and returns the base64 signature.
semantics: Signs a string with the game's built-in private key (MD5 + CryptSignHashA via Script::SignDataBase64) and returns the base64 signature. Needs argc==1 and arg1 a string with length>0, else int 0. Returns the EMPTY STRING (not 0) when: the story-data copy pointer vm+0x145c is NULL, or bit 0x10 of vm+0x12f0 is set (signing disabled), or Script::VerifyStoryFiles(vm+0x145c, vm+0x1460) fails (the loaded x3story data differs from the stock signature, i.e. modified scripts cannot sign). If SignDataBase64 itself fails (returns NULL) the result is int 0. Otherwise the base64 signature string. Side effect: CryptoAPI container creation.
notes: Handler 0x4af4fe (case 0x97). Used for high-score / statistics signing. 0 = bad arguments or crypto failure, '' = refused by the integrity check. An emulator running modified scripts should return '' (refusal).

name: SE_SaveAllTexts
summary: Writes every loaded text page of every language to a TSAV binary file.
semantics: Script::NativeSaveAllTexts (AP 0x004a52a0): path = text-directory format with file, opened "wb" (0 on failure). Writes "TSAV", 999, then for each of the 999 language slots its page count (0 if none) and the pages {pageId, count, entries {textId, strlen, bytes}} (big-endian words), then "/TSA". Returns 1. Real file-system side effect. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).

name: SE_LoadAllTexts
summary: Loads all text pages from a TSAV binary file written by SE_SaveAllTexts.
semantics: Script::NativeLoadAllTexts: path = pathTable text-directory format with file. Opens it (0 if missing), checks "TSAV", reads a slot count (big-endian; files from SE_SaveAllTexts have 999 = languages), then per language slot: page count, and if non-zero a NEW page hash map replaces vm.textPages[slot] (the old one is not freed), each page {id, count, entries {textId, length, bytes}}; checks the "/TSA" trailer (0 if missing, the loaded pages stay). Returns 1 on success. Texts are afterwards visible to SE_ReadText. Sync (handler resumes the task before Script::NativeDispatch AP 0x004ab880 / FL 0x004c84a0 returns).
bugs: AP 0x004a5940 (Script::NativeLoadAllTexts, FL 0x004c2a20; x3_src vm.cpp:2975 reproduces on purpose): the slot count from the file is not checked against the 999 slots (a corrupt file writes past vm.textPages), and an existing page map of a slot is leaked when it is replaced.
